description_text: Brown County State Park is Indiana's largest state park, known as the 'Little Smokies' for its rolling hills, dramatic fall foliage, and extensive hiking/biking trails.
campground_text: Main campground offers 401 electric sites (Buffalo, Raccoon, Taylor Ridge loops), modern bathhouses, camp store, plus a horseman's campground. RVs must use West Entrance.

description_text: Indiana Dunes State Park features majestic sand dunes rising nearly 200 feet above Lake Michigan, offering miles of sandy beaches and diverse trail habitats.
campground_text: Campground provides 140 spacious sites with 50-amp electricity, modern comfort stations, hot showers, and play areas within walking distance of the beach.

description_text: Turkey Run State Park features deep, sandstone canyons, old-growth forests, suspension bridges, and rugged hiking trails carved by ancient glacial meltwater.
campground_text: Offers 213 electric (Class A) campsites, wheelchair-accessible sites, modern restrooms/showers, dump station, and camp store.

description_text: Clifty Falls State Park features dramatic waterfalls, deep fossil-filled gorges, limestone cliffs, and hiking trails overlooking the Ohio River.
campground_text: Campground offers 106 electric sites and 63 non-electric sites, modern bathhouses, playground, and dump station.

description_text: Fort Harrison State Park features scenic walking trails along Fall Creek, a championship golf course, a historic military base museum, and popular sledding hills.
